intro: Most people use Claude one chat at a time. The owners getting the most out of it build a few things once, then use them every day. Here are the five I'd build first, in the order I'd build them, each with the prompt that starts it.

free.title: Build 1: A morning dashboard
free.body:
One page that shows what matters today: key numbers, the emails that need you, and your top three tasks.

Copy this inBuild me a one-page morning dashboard as an artifact. Sections: today's top 3 tasks, the 5 numbers I check every day ([e.g. leads, sales, cash]), emails waiting on me, and my calendar. Start with placeholder data, then tell me which tools to connect so it fills itself.

free.title: Build 2: A second brain
free.body:
Create a Claude Project called "Business Brain" and add your offer, prices, FAQs, best emails and SOPs as files.

Copy this inYou are my business brain. Answer only from the files in this Project. When something isn't in them, say so and tell me which document to add. First, list the 10 documents you'd want from me to know this business well.

free.title: Build 3: An executive assistant
free.body:
Connect your email and calendar to Claude, then give it a standing brief.

Copy this inEach morning: summarize my unread email in 5 lines, draft replies to anything a customer or partner sent (I'll review before sending), and plan my day around my calendar with 2 focus blocks. Never send anything without my OK.

free.title: Build 4: A marketing assistant
free.body: Copy this inUsing my business brain: give me 10 post ideas for this week based on the questions customers ask most ([list 3]), write the first 3 as ready-to-post captions in my voice, and tell me which of last month's posts did best and why. Here are their numbers: [paste]

free.title: Build 5: Your AI team
free.body:
Turn the builds above into roles. One Project per role, each with its own instructions: Assistant, Marketer, Researcher, Analyst. Start every role from this:

Copy this inYou are my [role]. Your job: [one sentence]. You report to me. Every day you deliver: [the output]. Ask me before spending money, contacting anyone, or deleting anything.

Keep a person in the loop: review anything that goes to a customer before it's sent.
